propositions: Identical inputs (same ticket, same code at HEAD, same criteria, same comments) yield non-deterministic verdicts across runs: PASS vs FAIL with no intervening changes, specifically on test-existence criteria

The verifier's test-existence judgment depends on the agent's variable free-form search strategy; when searches land on semantic/regex queries instead of ticket-id/literal-substring searches, the agent falsely concludes the test does not exist
The COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar payload lacks verified_at_sha, trace_id, and input context, making it impossible to distinguish genuine flakiness from input drift when analyzing stored records
Flaky FAILs block legitimate completions (expensive LLM retry loops); flaky PASSes undermine attestation integrity; both directions render the gate untrustworthy for certification
The verifier lacks pinned deterministic decoding (unpinned temperature causes sampling variance that compounds the search-strategy fallibility)
Test-existence false-negatives are the narrow empirical root: the verifier credits implementation but rejects criteria on lack of test confirmation, flipping between runs on identical code
